purpose: Assigned values for the 4-bit frame_class field of the MCL Link frame. This registry did not exist while values 0-9 were being assigned; it is created so that the namespace has one authority rather than a table inside a specification, and so that the 10-15 range has a stated allocation policy instead of being either silently free or silently closed.
field_width_reference: mcl-link/spec/link-v0.md section 3.1 -- link_major occupies the high nibble of the first byte and frame_class the low nibble, so the namespace is exactly 16 values and can never be widened without a new frame layout.

allocation_policy.0x0_0x9: Assigned. Dispositioned for Link major 1 by mcl-link/spec/link-class-disposition-v1.md.
allocation_policy.0xA_0xF: Unassigned. MCL Standards Action. A value here is refused structurally by any implementation that does not know the assignment. An implementation that DOES know it decodes the frame structurally and then refuses to act on it unless the contact negotiated its feature -- the two refusals happen at different layers, see two_layer_refusal below.

assignments.name: NEGOTIATION
assignments.contract: Link negotiation control, 7 bytes. Same specification.

assignments.name: DATA
assignments.contract: Canonical Wire Tier-0 object. Decodes identically to CONTACT; the distinction is intent.

assignments.name: NACK
assignments.contract: Fixed 4-byte control, same layout, carries a reason.

assignments.name: KEEPALIVE
assignments.contract: Empty payload. A receiver MUST accept one; nothing requires an implementation to send them.

assignments.name: ADAPT
assignments.contract: PERMANENT TOMBSTONE. MUST be refused on receipt, MUST NOT be emitted, and MUST NEVER be reassigned. Assigned for transport adaptation; nothing was built on it. Excluding it rather than reserving it would invite value 7 to mean something else later, and a peer that once meant 'adapt' by 7 would then be misread rather than refused.

compatible_addition.question: Does Link major 1 freeze the MEANINGS of the assigned values, or does it close the whole 4-bit namespace? Those are not the same statement, and the tree said both.
compatible_addition.resolution: It freezes the assigned meanings. The namespace stays open under the conditions below.
compatible_addition.basis: mcl-core/governance/ARCHITECTURE_CHARTER.md section 4 states that compatible evolution should prefer registry additions and new optional extensions, and that 'minor document revisions, new assigned values, errata, and compatible optional behavior do not consume a major wire version'. Assigning an unused value is a new assigned value; it reinterprets no existing canonical bytes, which is the thing section 4 says DOES require a new major.
conditions: The value is assigned here by MCL Standards Action, with a permanent specification reference.

Its use is gated by a negotiated feature bit, so a peer that has not advertised support never receives the class. The selection in mcl-link/spec/link-negotiation-v1.md section 6 is L.features & P.features, so a bit a peer does not know is a bit it did not set, and the AND clears it. Fail-closed is arithmetic here, not a rule anyone has to remember. The bit is enforced at the CONTACT layer, never inside the structural decoder -- see two_layer_refusal.
No existing class changes meaning, payload contract, or disposition.

An implementation that has not negotiated the feature does not act on the class. An implementation predating the assignment refuses it structurally, as an unassigned value; one that knows the assignment decodes it structurally and declines it at the contact layer. Unchanged major-1 behaviour either way, and no frame that means one thing today comes to mean another.
compatible_addition.consequence_for_the_disposition_spec: link-class-disposition-v1.md section 5 stated the decoder rule as 'frame_class > 9 -> reject'. That phrasing closes the namespace as a side effect of describing today's assignments. It is restated as 'frame_class not assigned, or assigned but not negotiated -> reject', which is IDENTICAL behaviour for every implementation that exists, and does not decide the 10-15 range by accident.
compatible_addition.not_yet_assigned: No value in 0xA-0xF is assigned by this revision. A SECURITY class is under design in mcl-link/research/security-carrier-design.md and deliberately spends no value: assigning one to a mechanism that might still change shape is how registries acquire tombstones.

two_layer_refusal.problem: An earlier revision of this registry said a newly assigned class is 'refused when assigned but not negotiated'. That is the right outcome and the wrong place. mcl_link_frame_decode() is deliberately a STATELESS structural decoder: it receives bytes and an output structure, and holds no contact, no negotiated feature set and no security state. Making it enforce a per-contact feature bit would push contact state into the codec to satisfy one rule, and that separation is worth more than the rule.
two_layer_refusal.structural_decoding: Is this class assigned at all, and is the frame structurally valid? Answered by the codec, from bytes alone. An implementation that does not know an assignment refuses it here -- which is exactly how a v1.0 implementation refuses a class added after it shipped.
two_layer_refusal.contact_admissibility: Did THIS contact negotiate the feature that enables this class, and is the class legal at this point in the contact? Answered by the contact layer, which is where the negotiated feature set already lives.
two_layer_refusal.consequence: The two questions have different answers for the same bytes depending on who is asking, and that is correct. A security-capable implementation structurally decodes an assigned SECURITY frame and then declines to deliver it to the security engine if the feature was never negotiated. An implementation that predates the assignment never gets that far: it refuses structurally, because to it the value is simply unassigned. Both refuse; neither needs the other's state.
two_layer_refusal.rule: A class assignment MUST NOT require the structural decoder to consult contact state. If enforcing a new class would need per-contact state inside mcl_link_frame_decode(), the assignment is shaped wrongly.

notes: The namespace is 16 values and cannot grow. Six remain. That scarcity is the reason this registry exists and the reason assignments are Standards Action only.
A reserved value is never reused. ADAPT is the worked example and REGISTRY_POLICY.md requires the same of every retired assignment.
This registry records assignments. It does not itself make class 10 legal; that needs an assignment plus a negotiated feature bit plus a specification.

governance.change_controller: The MCL maintainer (the owner of the eight MCL repositories).
governance.procedures: mcl-core/governance/GOVERNANCE.md section 4 defines application, review, promotion and deprecation for every MCL registry. They are defined once there rather than restated per registry, so they cannot drift apart.
governance.application: GOVERNANCE.md 4.1 -- an issue naming the registry, requested value, meaning, a permanent specification reference, the negotiated feature bit that gates it, and the failure behaviour required of a receiver that does not implement it. An application without a specification reference is not an application.
governance.promotion: GOVERNANCE.md 4.3 -- an Experimental Use value is NEVER relabelled Stable. This registry defines no Experimental Use range: the namespace is 16 values wide and cannot afford one, so every assignment is Standards Action and experimentation happens on a transport profile instead.
governance.deprecation: GOVERNANCE.md 4.4 -- a retired assignment becomes a permanent tombstone. Its value is never reused and a decoder must refuse it, because a peer that once meant something by that value would otherwise be misread rather than refused.
